question: What is the GIL in Python and how does it affect multithreading?

items.label: Q1
items.title: What is the GIL in Python?
items.text:
Question: What is the GIL in Python?
Source answer: The global interpreter lock lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time; CPU-bound threads do not run in parallel, I/O-bound threads still overlap waiting.

items.label: Q16
items.title: Design a rate limiter
items.text:
Question: Design a rate limiter
Source answer: Token bucket per API key in Redis: refill at rate r up to capacity B, take a token per request, reply 429 with Retry-After when empty. Sliding-window counters give stricter per-minute limits.

items.label: Q13
items.title: Why does TCP use a three-way handshake?
items.text:
Question: Why does TCP use a three-way handshake?
Source answer: Both sides must learn and acknowledge each other's initial sequence number; with two messages the server could not be sure the client received its sequence number, and stale duplicate SYNs could open connections.

question: How do I reverse a linked list in place?

items.label: Q7
items.title: Reverse a singly linked list
items.text:
Question: Reverse a singly linked list
Source answer: Walk the list keeping prev, curr and next pointers; point curr.next at prev and advance. O(n) time, O(1) space.

question: Redis 的 RDB 和 AOF 持久化有什么区别？

items.label: Q19
items.title: How does Redis persist data?
items.text:
Question: How does Redis persist data?
Source answer: RDB writes point-in-time snapshots; AOF logs every write and replays it on restart. RDB restarts faster and is compact; AOF loses less data.
